title: From 91 to one: Step-by-step guide to identifying 2026 Masters winner

elimination_steps.stat: Each of the last 46 winners had played in at least one prior Masters
elimination_steps.note: Only Fuzzy Zoeller (1979) won on debut. Recent runners-up Im (2020), Zalatoris (2022), Åberg (2024) could not close.

elimination_steps.stat: No one has won the Masters over age 50. High-water mark: Jack Nicklaus at 46 (1986).
26 of the last 28 winners had a prior top-30 at Augusta. Outliers: Zach Johnson 2007, Danny Willett 2016.

elimination_steps.criterion: Made Masters cut the year prior
elimination_steps.stat: Since 1998, all but one champion made the Masters cut the year prior. Exception: Patrick Reed 2018.

elimination_steps.criterion: Top-6 major finish in last 2 years
elimination_steps.stat: 14 of the last 16 winners had a top-6 finish in a major over the two preceding years.
Each of the last 14 Masters champions picked up at least 18 shots via SG:T2G in their four most recent starts.
16 of the last 17 winners ranked inside the top 50 in Driving Distance the year preceding their victory.
13 of the last 14 winners had 3+ career Tour wins. Exception: Danny Willett 2016.
Last 7 Masters champions each had an under-par scoring average at Augusta. DeChambeau sits at 72.54 (over par).
Only once since 2006 has the betting favorite won — Scheffler in 2024 (and Tiger Woods 2005).
Back-to-back Masters wins have happened only 3 times: Nicklaus 1966, Faldo 1990, Tiger 2002.

winner_summary: Solid Masters record, recent major success, length off the tee, ball-striking chops, promising recent form.
